response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior engineer (14+ years) with genuine strengths in distributed/event-driven systems, low-latency services, testing discipline, and developer tooling. However, the role's core requirement — modern hands-on C++/STL development — is represented by only ~7 months at National Instruments in 2014-2015 plus an academic project; the bulk of the career is web/backend work in TypeScript, Node.js, and DLang. There is no evidence of industrial automation domain experience, IEC 62443/SDL secure engineering, MQTT or industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850), or Azure. The transferable skills are real, but the gap against the primary technical and security requirements is too large for a mid-senior specialist hire.
strengths: 14+ years of broad engineering experience across embedded, backend, and web
Proven low-latency, concurrent, event-driven systems work (async I/O, fibers, microservices at scale)
Strong quality/mentoring culture: TDD, CI/CD, open-source test tooling, workshops and talks
concerns: Minimal and dated hands-on C++/STL experience (~7 months, 2014-2015)
No industrial automation, IEC 62443/SDL, or OT cybersecurity exposure
No evidence of MQTT, message brokers, Azure, or industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA)
